title: The Cold War
group: HIST-TOPIC — Overview Anchors (each links to deeper subdomains)
examples: What were the main differences between the US and the Soviet Union?
How did the Berlin Wall affect daily life?
What caused the Cold War to finally end?

explain.say: The Cold War was a period of tension between two major powers. These powers were the United States and the Soviet Union.

draw.text: US vs USSR: Cold War Tension

explain.say: The division of Europe was symbolized by the Iron Curtain. This phrase described the political boundary separating East and West.
A key crisis was the Korean War. This conflict showed the superpowers' deep ideological clash in action. It was a proxy war.
Another major flashpoint was the Cuban Missile Crisis. This event brought the world closer to nuclear conflict than ever before. It was a tense standoff.
The end came with the collapse of the Soviet Union. This marked the end of the bipolar world order. The USSR dissolved in 1991.
In everyday life, think about global trade today. Many countries still follow economic models influenced by the initial Cold War divisions. Trade routes often reflect these old power alignments.

faq.q: What exactly was the Iron Curtain?
faq.a: It was a symbolic and real boundary dividing Europe between Western and Eastern bloc countries. It represented the division between capitalist and communist ideas.
asks: Where did the Iron Curtain fall?
What did the Iron Curtain mean?

faq.q: Was the Cold War fought with actual fighting?
faq.a: No, it was called 'cold' because the major powers avoided direct military conflict with each other. They fought through proxy wars and arms races instead.
asks: Did the US and USSR ever fight directly?
What kind of fighting did they do?

faq.q: Why was the Cuban Missile Crisis so dangerous?
faq.a: It was dangerous because the placement of nuclear missiles brought the world to the brink of nuclear war. Both sides had advanced weaponry.
asks: What was the biggest threat of the Cold War?

faq.q: What does 'bipolarity' mean in this context?
faq.a: It means that the world's major power structure was dominated by two opposing poles, the US and the USSR. There were only two main global centers of power.
asks: What was the world structure like?
How many major powers were there?

faq.q: When did the Cold War officially end?
faq.a: The end is generally marked by the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991. This ended the major geopolitical conflict.
asks: When did the Soviet Union fall?

facts: The United States promoted capitalism and democracy during the Cold War.
The Soviet Union promoted communism and a single-party state.
The Berlin Wall physically separated East and West Berlin.
The Cuban Missile Crisis involved the threat of nuclear war.

quiz.say: The period of tension between the US and USSR was known as the:
quiz.why: This term specifically describes the long period of political tension without direct fighting.

wrong.0: World War Two was a period of direct fighting involving many nations.
wrong.1: The Great Depression was an economic downturn, not a superpower conflict.
wrong.2: This phrase is not the established historical term for the era.

quiz.say: The physical barrier dividing East and West Berlin was called the:
quiz.why: The Berlin Wall was the concrete structure built to keep people separated in Berlin.

wrong.0: While accurate, it is not the specific, famous name for the structure.
wrong.2: The Iron Curtain was a metaphorical boundary across a wider region.
wrong.3: This is not the recognized historical name for the barrier.

quiz.say: The collapse of which nation is generally seen as ending the Cold War?
quiz.why: The dissolution of the USSR removed one of the two main global powers.

wrong.1: China remained a major power but was not the primary catalyst for the end.
wrong.2: Germany was divided, but the USSR's collapse was the ultimate turning point.
wrong.3: Cuba was a flashpoint, but its status did not end the global conflict.
